# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the enrichment/categorization stage.

# Repository: `/app` — "transaction-enrichment-python" (bank statement transaction categorization service)

**Nature:** Python 3 Flask + pandas rule engine. No JS/npm. No tests exist in the repo (details in §4).
**Single git commit:** `047782b import codebase`. Tracked files: 52 `.py` + `Dockerfile` + `.gitignore` (54 total). No CSV/JSON/fixtures anywhere on disk (and `.gitignore` line ends with `*.csv`, so any labelled corpus would have been excluded).

## Layout

```
/app/Dockerfile                                        # gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
/app/.gitignore                                        # ignores __pycache__ and *.csv  (<-- relevant: fixtures would be untracked)
/app/categorizationapp/setup.py                        # pkg "categorizationapp"; deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4,
                                                       #   python-Levenshtein, fuzzywuzzy, gunicorn, scipy, sklearn, matplotlib
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py   # Flask app factory + request timing logs (30 lines)
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py # 936 lines: HTTP endpoints + per-bank dispatch
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/  # 35 per-bank scripts (no __init__.py; namespace pkg)
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/ # shared enrichment stages + regex constant banks
```

## Pipeline (the "enrichment stage")

`Controller.py` → `/categorizeTransaction` (line 69) does, per bank branch (the whole 91–932 block is the same 25-line body copy-pasted ~35 times):

1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)` — Controller.py:87
2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` → sets **`transactionCategory`** (NEFT/IMPS/UPI/CHEQUE_*/ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION/…), initial `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, and extracts **`partyName`** (counterparty) + `party2` (whitespace-stripped copy of partyName used for matching)
3. `card_clean_names()` + `card_purpose()` — only when `accountType == "CREDIT_CARD"`
4. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` — `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9`
5. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` — `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9` (counterparty canonicalization)
6. `internal_payment(...)` — `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8` (fuzzywuzzy match vs accountHolder)
7. `salary_detection(...)` — `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py:16` (Levenshtein + scipy hierarchical clustering)
8. optional `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()` when `isPFMEnabled == True`

Other endpoints: `/` (Controller.py:51), `/recurrentTransactions` (Controller.py:55 → `RecurrentTxns.recurrent_transactions`, `UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py:8`).

Every rule stage uses the same idiom: a Python list of `[boolean-Series condition, choice]` pairs → `pd.DataFrame(columns=['conditions','choices'])` → `np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default=…)`.

# 3. Test fixtures / labelled corpus with baseline expected categories & counterparties

**None exist.** Exhaustive checks performed:

- `git ls-files` → 54 files: 52 `.py`, `Dockerfile`, `.gitignore`. No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `conftest.py`, `fixtures/`, `data/`, `*.csv`, `*.json`, `*.jsonl`, `*.yaml`, `*.xlsx`, `*.parquet`, `*.sql`.
- `grep -ri "pytest|unittest|conftest|def test_|npm test|jest"` over `/app` → **no matches**.
- Only git commit is `047782b import codebase`; `git log --diff-filter=D` → no deleted files, so nothing was removed historically.
- No `.github/`, `.circleci/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Makefile`, `tox.ini`, `pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`.
- Nearest thing to "test artifacts": commented-out dendrogram plotting blocks labelled `# For testing purpose only` in `UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py:16–21` and `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py:27–32`.
- `.gitignore` ignores `*.csv` and `TEST*.xml` — strong hint that the original team held their labelled corpus as local CSVs and JUnit XML reports that were never committed.

So a baseline corpus must be created from scratch. The natural shape is `(bank, acc_type, description, remark, type, amount, balanceAfterTransaction, transactionDate)` → expected `(transactionCategory, transactionSubcategory, merchantType, partyName)`.

Required input columns (from the code, not documented anywhere): `description`, `type` (`"CREDIT"`/`"DEBIT"`), `amount`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate` (`%d/%m/%Y`, needed by `SalaryDetection.py:56`), and `remark` (used by `HDFC.py:100,214,215`, `Kotak.py:287`, etc.). Request payload keys: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]` (Controller.py:72–81).

        [transactions.description.str.contains("^OPENING BALANCE", na=False, case=False) , "OPENING_BALANCE"],

def run(bank, fn, rows, acc_type="SAVING"):
    mod = importlib.import_module('categorizationapp.BankScripts.'+bank)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['description','remark','type','amount'])
    df['balanceAfterTransaction'] = 10000.0
    df['transactionDate'] = '01/01/2021'
    df = clean_input_df(df)
    df = getattr(mod, fn)(df, acc_type)
    df = purpose(df, acc_type)
    df = clean_names(df, acc_type, bank)
    return df

out = {}
for bank, fn, rows in [('Canara','categorize_Canara_transactions',CANARA), ('PNB','categorize_PNB_transactions',PNB)]:
    df = run(bank, fn, rows)
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        out[f"{bank}|{r.description}|{r.remark}|{r.type}|{r.amount}"] = [r.transactionCategory, r.transactionSubcategory, r.merchantType, r.partyName]

steps.message:
All five findings traced to root cause and cleared. Every regression sat in exactly two bank scripts — `PNB.py` and `Canara.py` (the only two files whose mtime differs from the rest of the imported tree).

## Root causes and fixes

| Finding | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **F-1** cheque debit with bare-number note → `TRANSFER` | `PNB.py:60` matched `^[0-9]{5}$` on debits while the credit twin on line 61 matched `^[0-9]{5,6}$`; PNB instrument numbers are 6 digits (cf. lines 46, 55 which use `^[0-9]{6}`), so 6-digit cheque notes fell through to the default bucket | restored the debit rule to `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| **F-2** `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty `Micr Clg` | `Canara.py:164` only knew the `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` two-tag layout (field 2 = name); the MICR-clearing sibling fell to the generic `^CHQ PAID-` rule on line 165, which takes field 1 — the clearing tag | added `Chq Paid-MICR CLG` to line 164 so the name is lifted from field 2 |
| **F-3** plain NEFT credits → blank counterparty | `PNB.py:110` called `py_extract(..., pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)`; the pattern has a single capture group, so `.get(1)` returned `None` and `py_extract` fell back to `pd.Series("")`, which numpy broadcast as an empty name over every row hitting that fallback | `index=0` |
| **F-4** incoming IMPS P2A credit → sender name = reference number | `PNB.py:94` handled only `^IMPSOUTP2A` (name at slash-field 2). Inbound `IMPSINP2A` narrations dropped to the generic `^IMPS` rule on line 95, which reads field 3 — the trailing reference number | rule now matches `^IMPSOUTP2A\|^IMPSINP2A` |
| **F-5** ₹1 penny-drop credit → ordinary transfer | `Canara.py:19` guarded the account-verification rule with `amount.lt(1)`, which can never be true for a ₹1 token credit (sibling banks use `lt(2)`) | `amount.lt(2)` — a strict superset, so sub-rupee rows that already matched keep their label |

## Verification

- Reproduced all five symptoms first (clearing tag `Micr Clg`, blank NEFT name, `912345678901` as sender, `TRANSFER` on the ₹1 credit, `TRANSFER` on the 6-digit cheque note), then confirmed each now derives the baseline field.
- Ran an 85-row Canara/PNB fixture set through the full enrichment path (`categorize_* → purpose → clean_names`) before and after, and diffed all four derived fields. Only the intended rows moved; ordinary purchases, transfers, deposits, UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS layouts, ECS/auto-pay, charges and cash deposits are byte-identical.
- Confirmed end-to-end through the Flask `/categorizeTransaction` endpoint for both banks (43 and 42 rows, HTTP 200).
- Every fix is a widening or a restoration, never a narrowing, so no previously matching fixture can lose its label.

One consequence worth flagging for sign-off: because the PNB bare-note cheque rule sits above the POS/ECOM/interest/charges rules, any debit whose instrument note is exactly six digits is now labelled `CHEQUE_PAID` — the same precedence that already applied to five-digit notes and to the credit side. If the corpus contains card or e-commerce debits carrying a six-digit instrument number, that rule would need a guard rather than a widened quantifier.
